surface: observa: /apps/observa/ (Persuade), plus Read variants for /apps/observa/privacy/, /apps/observa/support/ and the 8 alternatives pages that target it (/alternatives/athlytic/, /autosleep/, /bevel/, /gentler-streak/, /hrv4training/, /oura/, /welltory/, /whoop/)

dossier.mechanism: Observa reads whatever Apple Health already holds (Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit). It scores every new day against your own rolling 60-day mean and standard deviation and tests each habit against each outcome until a pair clears n ≥ 10 and p ≤ 0.10. What comes back is one plain-English sentence with its n and confidence attached. All of it is computed on the iPhone or iPad, and nothing is uploaded.
dossier.audienceScene: The visitor wears an Apple Watch, Oura or Whoop, often trains, and sleeps with the device on. They have years of Health charts and no meaning from them. They check the phone right after waking, often in a dim room during a northern winter, or they land mid-day from a Google or AI answer for 'AutoSleep alternative' or 'what does my HRV mean'. Either way they are usually on a phone.
dossier.culturalHome: Quantified-self and endurance-training culture: r/AppleWatch, r/QuantifiedSelf, the HRV4Training, Whoop and Oura forums, and the sleep-science podcasts. It is a world fluent in HRV, RHR, deep sleep and 'readiness', tired of opaque 0–100 scores and suspicious of health data in the cloud. Its daily ritual is the phone check at the bedside or the kitchen window.
dossier.mustProve: Within one viewport, the page has to prove four things. Observa turns your own data into a sentence about you: a real-form insight with its n and confidence, labelled as a sample. That sentence is measured against your own 60-day normal, not a population average. It is computed on the device. And it is free to start ('Free — Pro from $2.99/mo'), with the official App Store badge and, on desktop, the QR.
dossier.categoryDefault: A dark navy or black dashboard: a floating iPhone mockup, neon activity and recovery rings, a 0–100 score dial, a glowing HRV line chart, a 'Your health, decoded' headline, a four-up feature-card grid and three pricing cards.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Soft pastel wellness: a cream or sage ground, rounded blobs, a serif 'Feel more rested' headline and sleepy moon illustrations, i.e. Calm/Headspace quiet.
dossier.literalReading: Observa reads as observe and observatory: telescopes, night sky, star fields. The icon already carries four small four-point stars. Only candidate #7 uses this reading.
evidence: _apps/observa.md: price.model freemium, price.value 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo'. Four plans: Free $0, Pro · Monthly $2.99/mo, Pro · Annual $22.99/yr (highlight), Lifetime $49.99 once ('Best long-term value', Family Sharing). Platforms iOS + iPadOS, status live, first released 2026-01-01, last updated 2026-07-11.

Absent: spotlight, comparison_table, roadmap, training_vocabulary, coach_cta, plateau_disclosure, creative_work, show_body.
ratings 4.1 from 12 (under 25), so no stars anywhere.
Icon: a folded ribbon heart running from apricot to ember on near-black, with four small four-point stars.

Screenshots are a dark navy UI in SF Pro with Apple system green/yellow/purple/orange. 1 Coaching: 'Recovery is moderate today. Based on recent patterns' plus status tiles Sleep Good / Recovery Fair / Activity Good / Heart Stable. 2 Correlations: dot-strength rows, 'Based on 128 days · Association, not cause'. 3 Circadian timeline (13.21 best coordination … 0.51 deepest sleep). 4 March heat-calendar + day-of-week bars. 5 Workouts: training load 32, acute:chronic 0.99. 6 Sleep: 87 ring, chronotype 'Morning Lark', sleep debt. The in-app wordmark is widely spaced lowercase 'o b s e r v a' in blue.

Journal posts in the developer's own voice: 'A chart with seven hundred datapoints and no overlay is not a tool — it's a Rorschach test'; 'never a single score, always the underlying metric measured against your own 60-day baseline'; 'Correlation is not causation… treat insights as hypotheses worth testing for two weeks'; 'three or four sentences a thoughtful coach might tell you'.

_data/transparency.yml: 0 tracking domains, 0 third-party SDKs, network calls none, data leaves device 'No', analytics none, no account. It lists the permissions as HealthKit read AND write ('save insights back to Apple Health'), which contradicts how_it_works step 1 'No writes.' The owner needs to resolve this before build.
_data/testimonials.yml: 5 hero quotes (Reddit H.P., O.A., I.D.; App Store C., and K. in French with an English translation). Usable verbatim; show no star values.
_data/app_enrichment.yml: 32 languages; recommend_when names AutoSleep / Bevel / Athlytic / Gentler Streak alternative searches.

8 alternatives pages assign app=observa (athlytic, autosleep, bevel, gentler-streak, hrv4training, oura, welltory, whoop). Each has a hero, quick_answer, a 4-point compare grid (scope, where compute happens, what you get back, account & pricing), 'when to pick' / 'when to keep' lists, FAQ and a CTA. 'Apple Health (for interpretation)' in alternatives_to has no page.

Incumbent (before/apps_observa-desktop and -mobile): cream ground, Newsreader H1, purple pre-headline, split hero with a dark phone on the right, badge + 'See how it works' button, pill row on mobile. Refused.

candidates.name: The weather bulletin: normals and anomalies
candidates.why: People read it in the same minute as their sleep data every morning. Meteorology's 'normal' (a fixed reference period) and 'anomaly' ('3° below normal') are exactly Observa's 60-day baseline and deviation. The forecast's '70% chance' is the one stated confidence the public reads daily. It carries the mechanism as calm one-line readings per body area (Sleep, Recovery, Heart, Activity, which are the app's own tabs), each against your normal with its confidence.

candidates.name: The explained chart: Health trend line with baseline band and annotations
candidates.why: Every wearer has scrolled Apple Health's HRV chart in what the developer calls a chart-trance, and the annotated explanatory graphic is the cure. It carries the mechanism literally: a ±1σ band for the 60-day baseline, the nights that leave it, and a leader line from each deviation to the sentence that explains it.

candidates.name: Nutrition Facts panel, re-referenced
candidates.why: Everyone knows it by heart, and Apple's App Privacy 'nutrition label' is Observa's own privacy proof. The panel's '% Daily Value' against a 2,000-calorie stranger becomes '% of your 60-day baseline'. That carries Observa's one move (the reference is you) in heavy rules and Franklin-style type.

candidates.name: Aneroid barometer with set hand
candidates.why: The hallway barometer already translates a measurement into words (Rain, Change, Fair). It also has a brass set-hand you align with yesterday's reading. The needle is today, the set-hand is your 60-day baseline, the gap is the deviation, and the dial word is the plain-English sentence.

candidates.name: ECG rhythm strip with machine interpretation line
candidates.why: Apple Watch ECG exports print on the pink millimetre grid under a classification line ('Sinus Rhythm'). That printed interpretation above a trace is the original sentence-from-signal. Its clinical register fights Observa's 'calm, not clinical' promise, though, so it ranks lower.

candidates.name: The temperature blanket: one knitted row per night
candidates.why: Knitters' one-row-per-day colour record, and the warming-stripes scarf, turned 'deviation from a reference' into something you can hold, and the icon is a folded ribbon. It carries the mechanism as sixty rows, each night dyed by how far it sat from your normal, so a recurring pattern shows in the cloth. Knitting's 'lifeline' thread is the baseline.

candidates.name: Observatory star atlas (literal reading)
candidates.why: The name and the icon's stars point straight here. An atlas plate plots points against a reference grid for a stated epoch. A constellation is a named pattern of points that are associated but not physically linked. That carries the mechanism as nights plotted against your 60-day baseline, with habit nights joined into a named constellation and astronomy's honest caveat: a pattern, not a cause.

styles.label: Atlas of Nights
styles.lineage: Printed star atlases: the engraved Didone lettering of Bode's Uranographia (1801) and Wil Tirion's Sky Atlas 2000.0 field plates (white stars on deep blue, a coordinate grid, a magnitude legend, Bayer Greek designations). Also the observer's red-light rule and the observing log.
styles.thesis: Your nights are stars plotted against your own 60-day baseline, and an Observa pattern is a constellation: a named shape of nights that belong together. As every star atlas admits, that is an association, not a cause. The page refuses the glowing score-ring dashboard.
styles.scene: In bed around 22:30 with the room dark, phone dimmed and Night Shift on, the visitor is deciding whether last night's sleep means anything. So the page is dark and dark-adapted: warm accents, no large bright fields.

styles.navigation: The cartouche is the microsite nav: the 'Observa' wordmark plus chart-index anchors (Sky · Catalogue · Method · Plans · Dark sky · Questions), which is the jump_nav set. styles.signatureInteraction: Draw the constellation. Three habit buttons under the sentence (Late leg day · Coffee after 14:00 · Screens in the last 30 min) redraw the apricot lines through that habit's nights on the same 60-star sky, using SVG stroke-dashoffset (700ms). They also swap the plate's metric label (deep-sleep share / resting heart rate) and reveal that habit's sample sentence from example_insights, with n and confidence where the data gives them (n=14 · 87%; n=23 · 91%). Without JS, the first constellation is drawn statically and all three sentences render as a list under the plate. With reduced motion, lines appear complete and the swap is instant.
styles.motionGrammar: Slow and astronomical. On first view the stars come out brightest-first over 1.2s (opacity only), then the constellation draws at constant speed. No twinkle, parallax or glow. Section reveals are 300ms opacity fades, gated by html.js with the 2.5s safety net, so content is never hidden without JS. With prefers-reduced-motion everything is static and visible at once.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages keep the cartouche and open with a 200px plate strip (grid and a scatter of stars, no constellation) carrying the H1 in Bodoni Moda 600 48px. The reading column is 66ch of Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 18/1.65 #E8ECF4 on #0E1C3A, with Mono for 'last updated'. On the privacy page, policy sections are catalogue entries. On the alternatives pages, the 4-point compare grid becomes a two-column catalogue table (Observa vs the competitor: scope, where compute happens, what you get back, account & pricing), 'pick Observa if' / 'keep X if' become two lists, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with a slim legend panel holding price and badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. The plate, grid and constellations are inline SVG built from an illustrative 60-value array kept in the page and labelled illustrative. The icon, screenshots and QR already exist.
styles.risk: This is the literal reading of the name and the most guessable direction. Dark navy with stars slides into a generic 'space' theme, or into the near-black-neon cluster, the moment anyone adds glow or twinkle. Didone on a dark plate can read as luxury fashion. The metaphor only lands if 'association, not cause' is printed next to every constellation. A night world may sit close to the sibling AfterShift.
styles.memoryTest: The sleep app whose page was a star chart: my late-leg-day nights were joined into a constellation, and it said constellations are patterns, not causes.

styles.label: The Morning Bulletin
styles.lineage: Public-service weather bulletins: the Finnish Meteorological Institute's readings against the 1991–2020 climate normal ('3° below normal'), the BBC Shipping Forecast's fixed spoken order of areas, the newspaper weather box, and the forecast's stated probability.
styles.thesis: This is a body bulletin, not a dashboard. Every reading is a calm sentence set against your own normal with its confidence beside it, and the numbers open only when asked. The opening has no charts at all, which refuses the score-ring dashboard and the floating phone.
styles.scene: A weekday at 06:45, standing at the kitchen window in grey northern daylight, phone in one hand and coffee in the other, checking the weather and last night's sleep in the same minute. That makes the page light.

styles.signatureInteraction: Sentence ⇄ numbers. Each bulletin row is a <details> whose summary is the sentence. Opening it shows the numbers the app reveals on tap (how_it_works step 5): a normal-range bar with a white ±1σ corridor on grey and one tick for the reading, labelled 'your 60-day normal (illustrative band)', plus the n, the window and the confidence. JS only animates the height (180ms) and slides the tick into place (240ms). Without JS, native <details> works fully. With reduced motion, rows open instantly and the tick is static.
styles.motionGrammar: Broadcast cuts, not fades. Sections appear without entrance animation. The only motion is row expansion, the tick settling into the normal band, and the sticky bar sliding in over 160ms. With reduced motion there are no transitions at all.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages read as bulletin notices. They keep the same header bar, set the H1 in Schibsted 800 48px, and add a one-line issue stamp (page type · last updated) in Public Sans 14px. The reading column is 68ch of Public Sans 18/1.6 on a white sheet over #F2F4F5. On the alternatives pages the compare grid becomes fixed-order rows (Scope · Where compute happens · What you get back · Account & pricing) with Observa and the competitor in two columns, 'pick Observa if' / 'keep X if' become two lists, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with the issue row (price and badge).
styles.risk: This is Impeccable's pick and the most familiar of the seven: 'readiness' and forecast language are already common in recovery apps. The craft has to live in the bulletin's typographic discipline, so no weather symbols are used. A chart-free opening may undersell the app's rich dark UI, which only appears from the fifth section. 'Forecast' implies prediction, so copy must say 'normal' and 'reading' and never promise future days. Watch the sibling Soon., which carries weather in its UI.
styles.memoryTest: The one that read like a morning weather bulletin ('Sleep: below normal'), where every line opened to show its numbers against my own normal.

styles.label: Sixty-Row Blanket

styles.thesis: Sixty nights, one knitted row each, every row dyed by how far that night sat from your own normal, so the pattern Observa finds is visible in the cloth. Making the data a textile you read by colour refuses charts and score rings.
styles.scene: A late Saturday morning, still in bed under the duvet with low winter sun across the covers, reading Observa's weekly reflection on the phone. That makes the page light.

ink: text on heather and apricot (11.3:1 on heather), focus ring
text on indigo, violet and rust bands; QR tile

type.display: Handjet (@fontsource-variable/handjet full file: wght + ELGR element-grid + ELSH element-shape axes, latin ~19 KB): H1 and section heads at 800, with the element shape tuned in build so letters read as rows of stitches
type.text: Familjen Grotesk 400/600 (variable wght, latin ~18 KB): all reading text, key labels, tables, price
type.utility: none; tabular figures from Familjen Grotesk for n, σ and prices
type.rationale: Handjet is an element-based typeface built so letters can be assembled from units such as stitches or cross-stitch, so the headlines here are knitted in rather than printed on. Familjen Grotesk, from a Stockholm studio, is a calm Nordic grotesk whose squared joins sit beside the stitch grid without competing. About 37 KB in total.

materials: Stockinette knit: an inline SVG V-stitch texture at ~6% contrast over flat yarn colours (text sits on the flat layer)
60 knitted rows, one per night, from a 5-yarn key
Woven labels: indigo patches with a dashed white 'stitched' border for the wordmark, the action and the care label
The lifeline: a single 2px apricot thread drawn through one row
Pattern-sizing tables (sizes across, amounts down) for the plans

The pattern in the cloth: example_insights.intro (stating these are sample cards), then the six insights as six full-width bands, each in the yarn of its direction (below normal indigo/violet, above normal apricot/rust, holding steady heather). Each band has the headline in Handjet 800 44px, the body in Familjen 18px, and the tag and n/confidence in tabular figures.

Lifeline: one sentence of analogy ('Knitters run a lifeline through a row they trust; your 60-day baseline is that row'), then how_it_works steps 1–6 numbered (HowTo) with the apricot thread running through step 2, then the four value_points as short sentences.

Yarn label, i.e. what it reads: the ten metrics as fibre content, a 'Spun from' line (Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit via Apple Health; ECG needs Apple Watch), and a 'Gauge' line (n ≥ 10 nights, p ≤ 0.10).
Off the needles: six screenshots in a scroll-snap strip on an indigo band, where the app's navy UI sits naturally, with captions in white Familjen. The six features follow as a two-column list.

styles.navigation: The woven-label wordmark plus six anchors (Blanket · Pattern · Lifeline · Plans · Care label · Questions), which form the jump_nav set. The current anchor gets a 2px apricot thread underline. On mobile, 'Contents' is a <details> list that also includes Privacy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: Re-dye against your normal. A two-state switch sits under the blanket. 'Against an average adult' colours all 60 rows against one population reference, and most rows collapse into one or two yarns: the flat, uninformative picture. 'Against your own 60 days' re-dyes the rows against your baseline. The late-leg-day nights then stand out in indigo, and the sentence 'You sleep 18% less deeply on days you train legs after 18:00 · n=14 · 87% confidence' appears beside them. Technically, a class on the blanket swaps a CSS custom property per row, and background-color transitions stagger top to bottom (6ms per row, 280ms each) like dye wicking. Without JS, both blankets render (side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile), each with its caption. With reduced motion the swap is instant.
styles.motionGrammar: Slow and vertical, like textile. The only choreography is the dye stagger running down the rows and the sticky ribbon rising over 200ms. Bands do not slide or parallax. Hovering a row outlines it with a 1px ink line, no shadow. With reduced motion there is no motion.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages keep the cast-off edge and the woven-label header. Under an H1 in Handjet 800 56px runs a 24px 'selvedge': the 60 rows compressed into one thin stripe. The reading column is 68ch of Familjen Grotesk 18/1.65 in ink on heather. Policy sections are set as care-label lines. On the alternatives pages the compare grid becomes a pattern-sizing table (Observa | competitor across; Scope, Where compute happens, What you get back, Account & pricing down), 'pick / keep' become two columns, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with a woven-label CTA patch holding price and badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. The stitch texture is an inline SVG pattern, and the rows are divs built from an illustrative 60-night array in two reference states, kept in the page and labelled illustrative.
styles.risk: It ranks sixth for resonance: knitting is not native to the quantified-self audience and can read craft-cute against a statistics app. The drenched multi-colour bands need strict AA pairing per band (rust and violet take white text only). Handjet is idiosyncratic and must stay at 40px or above. Both reference states are illustrative and must say so. Warm textiles can drift toward the spent cozy-cream palette, so heather and indigo must hold the ground, never cream.
styles.memoryTest: The striped-blanket page: one row per night, and when I switched from 'average adult' to 'my own 60 days' the colours rearranged and my leg-day nights stood out in indigo.

canon: Canon (the category played straight; not recommended): a dark-navy health dashboard with a floating iPhone at right showing a glowing recovery ring and score tiles, a 'Your health, decoded' headline over an App Store badge row, four-up feature cards, three pricing cards and an FAQ accordion.
notes: Dice: key 519bdbbc, assigned index 7 (the literal-reading candidate, last for resonance), so Style A is the star atlas. Reroll 1 gave 6, so Style C is the blanket. Neither roll was 1, so Style B is my #1, the bulletin. The roll ran degraded (no catalog challengers), as expected. The three signatures each prove a different leg of the mechanism: A shows correlation (draw the constellation), B shows translation (sentence ⇄ numbers, mirroring the app's tap-to-see-numbers), C shows the personal baseline (re-dye against your normal). Owner flags: (1) transparency.yml lists a HealthKit WRITE permission ('save insights back to Apple Health') while how_it_works step 1 says 'No writes.' Reconcile this before any page prints either claim. (2) ratings 4.1 from 12, so no stars. (3) founder.signals hard-codes '19 live apps', the one literal CLAUDE.md allows; keep it in sync. (4) 'Apple Health (for interpretation)' has no alternatives page, so render it as plain text. Fonts verified on npm: @fontsource/bodoni-moda, atkinson-hyperlegible-next, atkinson-hyperlegible-mono, schibsted-grotesk, public-sans, handjet (the ELGR/ELSH axes are in @fontsource-variable/handjet full) and familjen-grotesk. Each style's latin payload is about 37–79 KB. All demo data (the 60-night skies and rows, the normal-range bands) is labelled illustrative, and insight sentences come from example_insights labelled as samples.
